video_title: New Tech is Coming Online  | Barnett Koven
gist: Sponsored ChinaTalk conversation with Barnett Koven (MD of AI and data, Accenture Federal Services) on federal AI adoption: using entity resolution to unmask shell companies for export-control enforcement, a hybrid 'mostly traditional ML plus a sprinkle of GenAI' architecture to control token costs, the mismatch between two-year-ahead federal budgeting and unpredictable compute bills, and AFS's role building the secure data 'backbone' for DOE's Genesis Mission. The title's 'new tech coming online' is generic; content is about government AI implementation.

insights.claim: Koven says data and AI can improve export controls on two fronts, deciding what to control and measuring control effectiveness, against adaptive adversaries currently focused on advanced semiconductors and, to a lesser extent, critical minerals, where China has largely cornered supply.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Enforcement tooling, not just rule-writing, is a growth area for government AI spend.

insights.claim: Entity resolution that merges US government data with commercial corporate records such as Bloomberg and S&P data can reveal that an unknown shell company is linked, through seven corporate layers, to a PLA procurement arm.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Corporate-graph analytics is a key tool for catching export-control evasion.

insights.claim: Koven proposes predictive modeling of higher-risk entities for export control targeting, modeled on how Treasury's OFAC has long used past behavior to identify who to sanction next.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Sanctions-style risk scoring could expand to BIS export enforcement.

themes.theme: Data readiness and cost of AI

insights.claim: Koven estimates data engineering/cleaning share of high-end data science work has only fallen from about 80% to about 65% over five years because most government and commercial data still is not AI-ready.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Data plumbing remains the bottleneck and a durable services revenue pool.

insights.claim: LLMs can now do rote ETL and data cleansing at roughly a third or a quarter of the cost of five years ago, giving customers more incentive to finally clean their data and letting budgets fund projects about three times larger.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Cheaper data prep expands the addressable scope of AI projects rather than shrinking spend.
insights.quote: now I can do it at a third or a fourth the cost of what it was five years ago

insights.claim: A State Department NLP project analyzing roughly 3,000 diplomatic cables per day that took a half-dozen people six months could now be done by two people in weeks with current tools.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Illustrates order-of-magnitude labor compression in analytics work.

insights.claim: Koven argues enterprise and government AI should be 80-90% traditional deterministic AI/ML with generative and agentic AI applied only to niche parts, constraining token consumption and total cost of ownership while improving results.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Token demand from enterprise production use may be lower than 'throw tokens at it' assumptions imply.
insights.quote: that doesn't mean just throwing tokens blindly at the problem

insights.claim: Off-the-shelf models trained on the open internet underperform on niche government and corporate missions because the relevant sensitive data is not public, and garbage-in-garbage-out is exacerbated, making clean metadata critical.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Explains why labs partner with consultancies and PE firms for deployment.

insights.claim: Federal budgets are effectively set about two years in advance, which is problematic when token consumption and cloud compute bills are increasingly unpredictable.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Government AI spending will lag capabilities unless budget mechanics change.
insights.quote: your budget this year was decided two years ago, give or take

insights.claim: Koven recommends making AI budgets fungible across models, use cases and offices within a department, with FinOps controls for accountability.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Department-level compute pools would accelerate federal AI uptake.

insights.claim: Foundation model companies are releasing new models into FedRAMP unclassified government environments on the same day as public release, but classified environments lag due to security constraints including model-poisoning risks.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Classified-environment deployment remains a gating bottleneck for national security AI.

insights.claim: In model poisoning, the cost of offense rises linearly while the cost of defense rises exponentially, giving attackers an inherent advantage in classified settings.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: AI security for classified networks will be a persistent and growing cost.

insights.claim: Inaction on AI is itself risky because risk-averse US agencies are guaranteed to fall behind less risk-averse competitors, with China cited as the example.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Supports the case for accelerating government AI adoption despite risks.
insights.quote: In action is in and of itself risky.

insights.claim: Accenture Federal Services has about 15,000 employees serving only the US federal government, drawing on Accenture's roughly 800,000 global staff serving the Fortune 3000 to lift-and-shift commercial innovations into government.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Contractors with large commercial arms pitch themselves as the AI transfer channel to government.

insights.claim: To evaluate AI for strategic negotiations, Koven proposes giving the same prompts to a desk officer and the model: convergence may mean shared bias (mirror imaging), while divergence is where to interrogate for errors or novel insight.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: Human-baseline comparison is a practical eval method for high-stakes AI use.

insights.claim: Under DOE's Genesis Mission, signed at the White House by originally 26 companies including Accenture Federal, DOE is to become the US government's lead organization for generative AI, framed by clients as a Manhattan Project for the 21st century.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: DOE and the national labs become a central channel for federal AI spend.
insights.quote: we're going to treat advances in gen AI similar to the Manhattan Project for the 21st century

insights.claim: AFS is building a 'backbone for scientific research' to enable secure data sharing across national labs, DOE headquarters, NNSA and partners, pulling instrument data from equipment makers like Siemens with granular role- and attribute-based access controls.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: The bottleneck is connecting models to niche scientific data, not building better foundation models.

insights.claim: AI mining of discarded historical research and geological data could find new routes to critical minerals such as beryllium from previously uneconomic ores or mining tailings in places like Utah and Nevada.
insights.speaker: Barnett Koven (Accenture Federal Services)
insights.so_what: AI-enabled data reuse could aid US critical-mineral supply chain independence from China.
